reason: Distorted means misshapen, which is what deformed means.
A fig-shaped structure is pear-shaped (obovoid and narrowed to the base).
Narrow-necked only says the neck is narrow. Flask-shaped also says the body is swollen below, and that is not stated.
Petiolelike means resembling a petiole or stalk. Attenuate means tapering gradually to a point, which is a different thing.
Scarcely distinct (veins, margins and the like) means hardly visible, which is inconspicuous.
Single-rowed means uniseriate.
The bare word tearing does not mean fragile. It can describe how a part splits or opens, or the action of tearing. Fragile needs an explicit statement such as breaking easily.
A carrot-like part, usually a root, is conical and tapering.
A collar is a ring around an axis, so collar-shaped means ring shaped.
Covered with bristles means setose.
Drawn out (into a tip or point) is the same as attenuate.
Knob-shaped can describe a swelling anywhere on a part. Head-shaped is defined as abruptly enlarged at the tip into a rounded head.
Nodule-bearing means root nodules for roots. Leaf and stem nodules also occur, for example bacterial leaf nodules in Psychotria, so the rule should not apply to other parts.
Pulviniform means cushion-shaped, which is pulvinate.
Lenticelless means without lenticels, an absence of the lenticel entity.
Persisting for a long time means not falling off, which is non-deciduous. The word long is lost, but that is acceptable.
A maple-like leaf is palmately lobed. The leaf constraint is right.
A semi-shrub is a suffrutescent plant, and the whole-plant constraint is right.
Broom-like means many slender erect twigs, as in a broom. Virgate means wand-like, which is long, slender, straight and erect.
The rule loses the position (centrally). The statement says only that the part is not constricted in the middle.
Trigone is a variant of trigonous (three-angled).
Awn-tipped means an awn is present at the tip.
Thinly textured means thin in texture, which is decreased thickness.
Pinninerved means pinnately veined.
Rolled under (margins) means revolute.
Thin-coriaceous means somewhat leathery, which is subcoriaceous.
Pilulose is not a clear synonym of puberulous. It is rare and can mean bearing small ball-like bodies, so the mapping is doubtful.
Stegocarpic moss capsules have an operculum (lid), so presence of the operculum is right.
Flexuous means wavy or zigzag, which is sinuous, so not flexuous is not sinuous.
Without keels says the keel structure is missing. It does not say the shape is not keel-shaped. This should be an entity-absence rule, not a negated shape.
Lanuginous means woolly, which is lanate.
A bunchgrass grows in tufts, which is caespitose.
Lophate means crested or ridged. Ridged is the nearest term.
Inermous means unarmed, with no spines or prickles, so not spiny is right.
Keelless means no keel. It does not mean not keel-shaped, so it should be an absence rule.
Paniclelike means panicle-like.
Racemelike means raceme-like.
Exalbuminous means the seed has no albumen (endosperm).
Thickly textured means thick, which is increased thickness.
Rampant means vigorous and spreading unchecked. It does not mean creeping along the ground.
Biserial means in two rows, which is biseriate.
Delimited means bounded or marked off by a limit. It does not mean conspicuous.
Hoodlike means cucullate.
Not imbricate is the negation of imbricate.
Nigrescent means turning black or blackish. Black loses the becoming or tending part.
Pubescent-glandular is the same as glandular-pubescent, with the word order swapped.
Estipitate means without a stipe, so not stipitate.
Sheathed can mean enclosed by a sheath. Sheathing means wrapping round an axis. Not sheathed does not clearly negate the wrapping quality.
Shreddy normally describes bark that peels in shreds. The exfoliating term is for bark and axes, not other parts.
Linear-reticulate means marked with a network, which is reticulate. The linear detail is lost, but that is minor.
